$comment: Generated by make_vectors.py from reference.py. Do not hand-edit. SPEC.md 6.5: trade negotiation, optional feature 'negotiation', format 1.

protocol.$comment: The characteristic UUID is UUIDv5(PROTOCOL_NAMESPACE_UUID, 'characteristic:Negotiation'), recomputed here like the others in swu-v1.json. Card hashes are SPEC.md 6.2's, as in swu-v1.json.

catalog.note: Every identity a receiver in these vectors can resolve (SPEC.md 6.5.5), with its wire hash. Rejection vectors resolve against all of it; a scenario device resolves against all of it minus its catalogExcludes.

features.note: a peer with a newer format: use min(own, peer); unknown names are ignored

messages.note: SUGGEST, revision 1: a shared-numbering-era foil (SOR 19, same number as its standard) and a distinct-numbering-era foil (JTL 525, its own number); JTL 100 twice, in two conditions, as two lines ordered by (hash, condition)
SUGGEST at the 40-line maximum: 54 + 11 x 40 = 494 bytes, one attribute value
quantity 255 and no get lines: the wire carries 1..255 whatever an app's screens allow, and a gift is a valid suggestion
condition 9 is reserved: valid on the wire, read as 0 (not stated)
ACCEPT of the first SUGGEST: its digest is FNV-1a 64 of that message's bytes from offset 52
DECLINE, reserved reason 7: valid, read as 0

receipts.note: reserved status 0x0C: a failed delivery, never OK

invalidReceipts.note: empty: read before any write on this connection: not a receipt, a failed delivery
20 bytes: not a receipt, a failed delivery
22 bytes: not a receipt, a failed delivery
format 2: not a receipt, a failed delivery

lineNormalization.note: same (hash, condition) merges by adding quantities; result ascending by (hash, condition)
one hash with two finish bytes: refused

rejections.note: format 2, a single byte: the format is judged before the length
SUGGEST one byte short of 54 + 11 x lines
SUGGEST with one trailing byte (no extension bytes exist)
give lines not ascending by hash
one hash in two conditions, in descending condition order
finish byte 2: swu has two finishes
finish byte 1 (foil) on the hash of a standard card: the hash decides the card
a canonical card the receiver's catalog does not hold
detail counts distinct unknown hashes (2); unknown cards are judged before a finish mismatch

scenarios.note: Plain data. For each scenario, create one device per entry in 'devices' (state IDLE, the given session id and matches, catalog minus catalogExcludes), then feed every step's event to its device in order and compare the output and the state snapshot. Event types: suggest, accept, decline, end, stop, retry, tick, matchPruned (local); incoming (a value written to Negotiation, on a connection whose central wrote Info with id connectionInfoId); delivery (the receipt read back, or a local failure). 'now' is in seconds. Output: send (bytes to deliver), receipt (bytes the receiver stores for the read), att (an ATT error, no receipt), refused (a local action not allowed in this state; nothing changes).

list.name: suggestAccept
list.note: A suggests, B accepts; both end ACCEPTED.

steps.note: L1 from IDLE: a new negotiation, revision 1
B shows the suggestion mirrored
L2: ACCEPT carries the digest of A's SUGGEST body
the author is the sole arbiter: A is ACCEPTED on receipt
ACCEPTED is terminal: a new suggestion opens a new negotiation

list.name: counterDecline
list.note: Counter, decline, and a new suggestion after a decline.

steps.note: B counters: revision 2, author B
A declines revision 2
B is DECLINED_BY_PEER
only the non-author may accept, and only RECEIVED
B sends revision 3

list.name: crossingSuggests
list.note: Both change the suggestion at once: two SUGGESTs at revision 2. Rule 2: A's session id is smaller, so A's wins on both phones.

steps.note: A changes its own pending suggestion: revision 2
at the same time B counters: also revision 2
A holds its own revision 2 and wins the tie: SUPERSEDED
B holds its own revision 2 and loses the tie: A's replaces it
B is told its suggestion was replaced; it already shows A's

list.name: bothOpenAtOnce
list.note: Both open a negotiation with each other at once, under different ids. Rule 2 on (revision, author): A's wins and its id is kept.

steps.note: A's own revision 1 wins: SUPERSEDED
B adopts A's negotiation id
the receipt for B's abandoned negotiation is ignored

list.name: acceptCrossesCounter
list.note: B accepts revision 1 while A replaces it with revision 2. A committed revision 2 first (Rule 1), so B's ACCEPT is STALE and B is shown revision 2.

steps.note: ACCEPT of revision 1, but A's current is revision 2: STALE
STALE while ACCEPTING: back to RECEIVED, revision 1 still current
revision 2 arrives and supersedes

list.name: lostReceipts
list.note: A receipt is lost; the sender retries the identical bytes and gets DUPLICATE, which it treats as OK. Shown for a SUGGEST and for an ACCEPT.

steps.note: B applies it, but A never reads the receipt
A only knows delivery failed
the retry sends the same bytes
DUPLICATE: nothing changes on B, A counts it as delivered
A is ACCEPTED; the receipt is lost
B stays ACCEPTING
DUPLICATE: B becomes ACCEPTED too

list.name: cancel
list.note: Ending a negotiation, and a CANCEL that arrives after an accept.

steps.note: L4: A ends the trade
B is CANCELLED
nothing left to accept
a new negotiation
A is ACCEPTED; B's receipt read is lost
B ends while ACCEPTING
CANCEL after ACCEPTED: CLOSED, A stays ACCEPTED. Each user still confirms (or not) their own collection change

list.name: expiry
list.note: 10 minutes without a message expires a negotiation (reference value); a pruned match expires it too.

steps.note: not yet
600 s since A's last message: EXPIRED, CANCEL best effort
B's own timer fires too
B already expired it: CLOSED
and the other way round
B pruned its match with A

list.name: busy
list.note: B is in a negotiation with A; C's suggestion is BUSY.

steps.note: BUSY; B's negotiation with A is untouched

list.name: unknownCards
list.note: B's catalog lacks a card in A's suggestion: UNKNOWN_CARDS, nothing is shown to B.

steps.note: detail = 1 unresolvable hash
B never had this negotiation: CLOSED

list.name: unsupported
list.note: A peer without the feature, and a message in a format the receiver does not implement.

steps.note: the peer has no Negotiation characteristic: a local result, nothing was written
format 2: UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT, detail = highest format B implements (1); id and revision echo as zero

list.name: senderChecks
list.note: Messages that are not addressed to the receiver, or not from a current match on this connection.

steps.note: to = C: NOT_FOR_ME
from = A, but the Info written on this connection was C's: UNKNOWN_PEER
C is not one of A's matches: UNKNOWN_PEER

list.name: rateLimited
list.note: A second message from the same peer within 1 s is RATE_LIMITED (reference value); the retry a moment later is applied.

steps.note: one outbox per side: nothing new until the previous receipt
A changes its suggestion straight away
0 s after B applied the previous message from A
the outbox is still undelivered: same bytes again
